issues.problem: Typed text that has not been written yet is tied to a fixed (row, column) index. Foreign commits to the same table (an AI or plugin table.edit, a collaborator, or edit.undo run from the shell's ⌘Z key command or the toolbar Undo, which skip TableUndoManager) do not move the edited cell or the pending setCell. modelChanged also lays the local text over whatever cell now sits at the old index, and flushTyping then writes the whole cell to that index. Example 1: a 2×2 table, the user types in (1,0) ('A2' becomes 'A2x'), and another principal runs insertRowBefore row 0 within 350 ms. The overlay hides 'A1' under 'A2x' and setCell(1,0) overwrites 'A1', while the real A2 cell (now row 2) keeps its old text. Example 2: the user types in (0,1) while another principal merges (0,0)-(0,1). The edited cell is now covered, so apply() moves editing to the anchor, and setCell(0,1) resolves to the anchor and replaces the merged 'A1\nB1' with 'B1x', so 'A1' is lost. Example 3: ⌘Z within the debounce undoes the step before the pending one. The overlay masks the reverted text, and the pending write puts it back and clears redo, so the undo seems to do nothing, or it removes a just-inserted row and the pending text fails with 'row outside the table'.
issues.fix: Remember the undo groups this view issues (typingGroup and each edit()/enqueue group). In commitsArrived, handle a changeset whose group is not one of them and whose mutation is `.block(doc, before, after)` for this block as follows. (1) If before?.table and after.table differ in row count, column count, row or column order, or merges, remap `editing` and `pendingText?.cell`. Match the edited row by the longest common prefix and suffix of before.rows and after.rows, and do the same for columns. For a move, find the before row among the after rows by its other cells. Re-anchor through TableOps.anchor. If the cell was deleted or became covered, end editing and drop the pending text, with no write. (2) If the changeset's command is edit.undo or edit.redo, or it changed the edited cell's text (before cell != after cell), cancel commitTask, set pendingText = nil, and reload the editor from the model instead of overlaying. Write setCell with the remapped position. Add view tests with a Harness: type into (1,0) through textViewDidChange, run `table.edit insertRowBefore row 0` with h.run before `flushEdits()`, and assert (2,0) holds the typed text and (1,0) still holds the old row 0 text. Add the same check for a foreign merge, and one for `h.app.bus.undo(doc)` before the flush, asserting no setCell is written afterwards (undoDepth unchanged, canRedo true).

issues.problem: This is a perf and memory problem on large tables. Tables may be up to 250 × 30 (7,500 cells). Each visible cell gets its own UIButton and UILabel, created for the whole table whether or not it is on screen, with no virtualization. The editor caches one TableBlockView per block, so all of them stay alive. Every keystroke runs relayout over every cell and then placeViews over every cell. placeViews re-sets frames, compares and re-assigns label text, sets backgroundColor, calls setNeedsLayout on every TableCellView, recomputes plainText twice, and does two String(localized:) lookups per cell. It also rebuilds the border path and the accessibility element array. A filled 250 × 30 table therefore costs tens of milliseconds or more per character typed, and keeps thousands of label backing stores resident while any part of the table is on screen. Small tables are fine, but the documented maximum lags while typing and risks memory pressure on iPhone.
issues.fix: (1) In textChanged, re-measure only the edited cell's span. If layout.rowHeights for its rows is unchanged, update only editor.frame and skip relayout. Otherwise rebuild TableGridLayout with the new row height and move frames only. (2) Give TableCellView a `shown: (RichText, RGBA?)` key and call show(...) and setNeedsLayout only when it changes. Hoist the two localized hints out of the loop. (3) Create cell views only for rows that intersect the visible rect of enclosingScrollView() converted to grid coordinates, plus one screen of margin. Observe that scroll view's contentOffset (KVO in subscribe, removed in unsubscribe) to add or recycle views from a pool. Keep the accessibility data-table protocol answering from the model, so VoiceOver still reaches every cell. (4) Add a CI-asserted test: build a 250 × 30 table filled with text, type 20 characters through textViewDidChange, and assert elapsed < budget × 4 (for example 16 ms × 20 × 4) and `cellViews.count` far below 7,500 for a 600 pt visible rect.

issues.problem: This is a trust-boundary gap in CSV export. Cell text written by plugins, the AI or collaborators is exported unescaped, so a field such as `=HYPERLINK("https://evil","x")`, `+cmd|' /C calc'!A0` or `@SUM(...)` runs as a formula when the CSV from Share & Export or table.exportCSV is opened in Excel or Numbers. The ponytail note keeps it to let negative numbers round-trip, but that does not need the full exposure.
issues.fix: In csvField, prefix a single quote (and then quote the field) when the text starts with '=', '+', '@', '\t' or '\r', or with '-' not followed by a digit or '.' (so -5 and -0.5 still round-trip). Add cases to testCSVQuotesUnicodeMultilineAndMergedTextExactlyOnce for `=1+1`, `@x`, `-5`, `-x`, and a lone '\r' inside a field.

issues.problem: The header says that a merged cell's text and background live in its anchor and that covered cells stay empty. This is not enforced. setBackground writes the colour into every covered cell (merge a 1×2 range, set (0,0) to red, split, and both cells are red), normalized() keeps text that plugins or AI put into covered cells, and isConsistent does not check either. A later merge of a larger range then brings that hidden text back into the anchor.
issues.fix: Either enforce the invariant or drop it from the comment. To enforce it, have setBackground write only to TableOps.visibleCells inside the expanded range, and have normalized() move non-empty text from covered cells into the anchor (appending paragraphs) and clear covered cells' text and background. Also check this in isConsistent. Add TableOpsTests for setBackground on a merged cell followed by split, and for normalized() with text in a covered cell.

issues.problem: Text typed within the last 350 ms is held only in memory until the debounce fires. If the app is backgrounded in that window and then terminated while suspended, that text is lost, because leaving the app does not remove the view from its window and nothing flushes it.
issues.fix: In subscribe(), also sink `UIApplication.willResignActiveNotification` and `UIScene.willDeactivateNotification` (receive(on: main)) to `self?.flushTyping()`. In flushTyping, wrap the enqueued write in `UIApplication.shared.beginBackgroundTask` / `endBackgroundTask`, skipping it when NibApp.isHostlessTest.

issues.problem: Several risky paths have no tests. The pure drag-reorder and resize geometry (TableLayout.nearestBoundary, moveDestination, TableGridLayout.divider(near:slop:)) is untested. Nothing tests that TableMenus.sections offers Merge versus Split versus nothing for a range, or that menus are read-only in read-only documents. The view's reaction to commits (modelChanged keeping the caret and clamping selection after rows are deleted) and table.edit insert/delete with count > 1 through the command are not covered either.
issues.fix: Add XCTest cases for the following. moveDestination(source: 2, boundary: 4) == 3 and nearestBoundary at midpoints. divider(near:) picks the closest right edge within slop and nil outside. sections(for: .cells(range)) contains 'merge' for an unmerged 2×2 range, 'split' for an existing merge, and no insert, delete or background entries when readOnly is true. Run h.run deleteRow {row: 0, count: 2} on a 3-row table, check undo restores it exactly, and check that a TableBlockView editing row 2 ends at row 0 afterwards.
